title: Fault Decomposition Viewer — interactive failed-request decomposition for Console
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and prototype a new Console panel — Fault Decomposition Viewer — that surfaces a structured, interactive breakdown for failed or retried requests. The goal is to let engineers and SREs quickly answer: what failed, where in the stack it failed (client / routing / runtime / model), whether retries changed the outcome, and which request payload elements (prompts, function inputs, metadata) correlate with errors.

Why this exists:
- Observability for failed requests today is fragmented: traces, raw logs, and the request table are separate and require manual correlation.
- We want a single focused view that reduces MTTI for LLM failures and supports root-cause triage, customer-facing incident notes, and model quality regressions.

Key screens & components (proposed):
- Top header summary: single-line failure classification, primary error code, first-seen timestamp, # retries, latency, model variant. Quick actions: open GitHub PR, add to incident, copy request ID.
- Request timeline lane: visual waterfall showing original request → retries → fallbacks (model variants, region routing), with hover to show exact payload and token counts.
- Payload inspector: side-by-side diffs for prompt and function args across retries (highlight changed keys, redline removed/added tokens, label fields that appear correlated with failure).
- Error taxonomy lens: stacked badges that map provider/runtime error -> Redwood classification (e.g., client-rate-limit, kernel-oom, kv-cache-miss, decoding-error). Clicking a badge filters timeline & logs.
- Execution trace: expandable rows for stages (ingest, routing, serving runtime, kernel exec, postprocess) with metrics and SVG mini-graphs (latency breakdown, memory).
- Token heatmap (optional): per-token error signal for decoding failures or toxicities.
- Related-events pane: linked requests (same customer, same prompt hash), recent rollouts affecting the model/version, and a checkpoint to console's rollout history for quick rollback context.

Prototype links and assets:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/console-fault-decomposition (v3 prototype with interactions)
- Clickthrough video (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/fault-decomp-proto-v3.mp4
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Fault+Decomposition+Viewer+PRD
- Early implementation spike: GitHub PR #4127 (eng/runtime): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127

Design decisions & trade-offs:
1) One-pane vs two-pane layout: two-pane (timeline + payload/trace) chosen to keep temporal context visible while inspecting payload diffs. Mobile will collapse to a stacked view.
2) Error taxonomy mapping: we keep both upstream (runtime/provider) and Redwood-normalized classifications to reduce cognitive load when debugging cross-environment failures. This required adding a small mapping table in metadata emitted by the runtime (ENG dependency).
3) Performance vs fidelity for token heatmap: token-level coloring can be expensive when rendering large prompts. Heatmap is paginated and off by default; enabled via a toggle in the header.
4) Data retention: payload diffs of customer data are sensitive — design defaults to masked PII and requires admin opt-in for raw payload access. See security notes in PRD.

Accessibility & UX constraints:
- All color indicators include textual labels and icons; tooltips available on hover and keyboard focus.
- Timeline is keyboard-navigable; payload diff supports screen-reader-friendly summaries ("tokens changed: 14; field removed: customer_email").

Acceptance criteria (must meet before Merge/Release):
- Prototype validated with PM + 2 SREs and 2 customers in usability test (notes attached).
- Figma prototype flows for at least: single failure, multi-retry with fallback, model variant change, kv-cache miss.
- Console API surfaces required metadata (error classification, stage timings, payload snapshots) — ENG-2891 provides schema; integration smoke test passes.
- Security review signoff on payload masking strategy (if opt-in required).
- Performance: panel open time < 450ms for typical request payloads (<= 4KB) in staging.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Should rollout widget include a direct rollback button for approved enterprise accounts? (PM says yes for Dedicated customers; legal/security to validate.)
- How to prioritize long-running requests that produce incremental token events? We propose collapsing token events into ranges unless the user expands the token heatmap.
- Which retries to show by default? We show first, last, and any explicit fallback variant (configurable via timeline settings).

Next steps (this ticket):
1) Finalize high-fidelity screens and hand off to frontend eng for spike implementation of timeline rendering and diffing component (Rory assigned).
2) PM to schedule usability sessions with Pilot customers next week (Emily Royce).
3) ENG to implement and expose mapping table fields required for taxonomy (dependent work ENG-2891).

Notes from prototype usability sessions (summary):
- SREs liked combined timeline + payload but asked for a clearer legend for retry semantics.
- Two customers requested an export-to-incident feature that includes payload diffs and a short human-readable root-cause suggestion (follow-up PM/Eng work).
- One engineer noted long diffs for multimodal prompts; suggested collapsing binary blobs into summarized placeholders.
